subject: Post-demo: platform instrumentation checklist & next validation tests
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nimbuscloud.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:22:00 -0000
Subject: Post-demo: platform instrumentation checklist & next validation tests

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the candid run-through of your eval goals. Quick recap from our side plus proposed next tests so we can close the instrumentation and ops comparison for your procurement review.

TL;DR: Redwood can run the exact telemetry and tracing tests you asked for in a shared sandbox (short-lived account) and provide a side-by-side matrix with the hyperscaler endpoints you're testing. We recommend the three validation passes below to prove cost/latency/observability parity.

Summary of differentiators discussed
- Prefix/KV cache visibility: we can surface per-request cache hit/miss metrics (latency and token savings) so you can quantify cost delta vs stateless endpoints.
- Request-level tracing: OpenTelemetry-compatible traces with token-level timing and kernel-stage annotations (warm/cold KV, attention kernel).
- Rollout controls & graceful fallback: can route by region/capacity and auto-fallback to quantized variants with preserved API surface.
- Cost controls: built-in batching and throttling suggestions per workload; we’ll show expected unit-cost improvements for your inference mix.

Proposed validation tests (we can run these in the shared sandbox; see attached matrix)
1) Observability parity check (Day 1)
   - Goal: confirm comparable trace granularity and dashboarding for request -> token timeline
   - Steps: run 1k requests (1–5 concurrent clients) with 512-token responses; capture traces, dashboard panels (latency by stage), and a 48h retention export
   - Success criteria: traces show token timing + ability to filter by model variant and by route

2) Throughput & batching behavior (Day 2)
   - Goal: measure end-to-end throughput with continuous batching vs hyperscaler batch endpoints
   - Steps: synthetic load (50–200 RPS spikes), measure p50/p95/p99 tail, per-token cost estimate, and effective batch sizes observed in traces
   - Success criteria: p95 within your SLO and token-cost estimate within the target band provided in call

3) Security/compliance check (Day 3)
   - Goal: verify audit logs, request-level metadata retention, and KMS-wrapped keys for sandbox artifacts
   - Steps: enable audit logging, request log export, and run a sample key-rotation flow
   - Success criteria: audit events contain request id, model hash, and principle; keys rotate without breaking running KV cache sessions

Asks from your side (to unblock sandbox setup)
- One sandbox admin (email) to provision temporary credentials.
- Shortlist of 3 canonical prompt templates you want traced (we’ll attach trace IDs).
- Confirmation on retention window for exported logs (48h default; can extend to 7d for test).

Next steps
- If okay, we’ll provision the sandbox by EOD Wednesday and run Day 1 tests Thursday morning.
- Follow-up 45-min sync Friday to review dashboards and share the matrix (I’ll invite your security contact if you want them on the call).

Attachments: Redwood instrumentation matrix (spreadsheet), sandbox instructions (text)

Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt

Subject: Re: Post-demo: platform instrumentation checklist & next validation tests

Thanks, Hannah — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A few quick clarifications before you spin up the sandbox: 

- Retention: 48h is fine for the initial run. We may request a 7d window for the throughput day if the results need further digging.
- Security: our security lead (Priya) will want to confirm KMS integration details and proof of key isolation for the sandbox. Can you share the KMS provider options you support?
- Logging: we need the logs to contain user-id and session-id fields (PII redaction is fine for the rest). Will your audit export include these fields?

We can provide the three prompt templates by tomorrow morning. For sandbox admin, assign the account to me (alex.morgan@nimbuscloud.io) and I’ll route access to our SREs.

Happy to do the Thursday morning Day 1 tests — what timezone are you scheduling in? PT works for us.
